sources.entry: Go: _Build Your Own Redis from Scratch_

summary.title: Build Redis from scratch
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a simplified in-memory, Redis-like database in Go, covering a RESP parser, concurrent connections, and Append Only File (AOF) persistence.
takeaways: Build a Redis-like server in Go supporting string and hash commands
Write a parser for RESP so the server can receive commands and send responses
Use goroutines to handle multiple client connections at the same time
Persist data to disk with an Append Only File and restore it after a restart or crash
summary.summary: This is a multi-part article series that walks through building an in-memory database similar to Redis, written in Go. It supports a subset of Redis commands for strings and hashes, with the code split into four files (aof.go, handler.go, main.go, resp.go). The series explains the RESP protocol parser, concurrent connection handling with goroutines, and AOF-based persistence to restore data on restart. The author notes that it is written with simplicity in mind, and readers need basic Go and some Redis familiarity, though the page says beginners can still benefit.
